Judge whether the copy matches the brand voice.
Voice guidelines: ['Write plainly and specifically; name the feature and what it does.', "Lead with the customer's trip, not the product's ego.", 'Prefer concrete numbers (weight, capacity, ratings) over adjectives.', "Respect the reader's experience; assume they know the outdoors.", 'Be honest about limits — say what the gear is not built for.', 'One clear call to action per message.']
Tone descriptors: ['grounded', 'practical', 'warm', 'understated', 'trail-tested', 'unpretentious']
Terms to avoid: ['guaranteed', 'miracle', 'risk-free', 'best ever', 'cure', '100% safe', 'unbreakable', 'lifetime warranty', 'revolutionary', "world's best", 'bulletproof']
Subject: What our staff is actually packing this winter
Preview: No hype. Just the gear sitting in our own packs right now.
Body: Hey,

Every winter our team puts together a short list of what we're personally reaching for — not what's new, not what's on sale, just what's been earning its place in the pack.

This year we ran into a snag: our catalog is currently being updated, and we don't want to point you at products we can't fully stand behind with accurate details. That's not how we do things.

Check back with us in the next few days. The staff picks list will be live on the site once we've confirmed every fact — weight, materials, what each piece is built for, and honestly, what it's not built for.

We'd rather wait and get it right than rush you toward something based on our say-so alone.

Thanks for being patient. We'll have something worth reading in your inbox soon.

— The Northbay Supply Team
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences. Reason first, then decide — the verdict must follow from the reasoning. Use exactly this key order: {"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...], "score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail"}.
